```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

CATEGORIES = ["Electronics", "Clothing", "Home Decor", "Automotive", "Books"]

def task_func(s1, s2):
    s1 = pd.Series(s1)
    s2 = pd.Series(s2)

    # If values are already category-labeled, reindex by the predefined categories.
    # Otherwise, assume the inputs are in the same order as CATEGORIES.
    if set(CATEGORIES).issubset(set(s1.index)) and set(CATEGORIES).issubset(set(s2.index)):
        s1 = s1.reindex(CATEGORIES)
        s2 = s2.reindex(CATEGORIES)
    else:
        s1 = pd.Series(s1.values, index=CATEGORIES[: len(s1)])
        s2 = pd.Series(s2.values, index=CATEGORIES[: len(s2)])

    mask = (s1.index.isin(CATEGORIES)) & (s2.index.isin(CATEGORIES))
    s1 = s1.loc[mask]
    s2 = s2.loc[mask]

    qualified = [cat for cat in CATEGORIES if cat in s1.index and cat in s2.index and pd.notna(s1[cat]) and pd.notna(s2[cat]) and s1[cat] > 200 and s2[cat] > 200]

    if not qualified:
        return None, 0.0

    vals1 = s1.loc[qualified].astype(float)
    vals2 = s2.loc[qualified].astype(float)

    distance = float(np.linalg.norm(vals1.values - vals2.values))

    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    x = np.arange(len(qualified))
    width = 0.35

    ax.bar(x - width / 2, vals1.values, width=width, label="Store 1")
    ax.bar(x + width / 2, vals2.values, width=width, label="Store 2")

    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels(qualified, rotation=45, ha="right")
    ax.set_ylabel("Sales")
    ax.set_title("Sales Comparison for Categories Above Threshold")
    ax.legend()

    fig.tight_layout()
    return ax, distance
```
